title: Acceptance from equal reachability counts
statement: Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input alphabet, let $L$ be a language of Boolean strings, and let $sp$ assign a natural-number space bound to each input length. Suppose that for every input $y$ there is a time $T$ such that every choice string of length $T$ makes $N$ halt, every such run uses at most $sp(|y|)$ work-tape cells, and $y\in L$ exactly when some such run halts with output $[\mathrm{true}]$. Fix an input $x$ and a window size $s$, and suppose the sets of codes reachable from the initial configuration by zero or more steps within the $s$-window and within the $(s+1)$-window have equal cardinality. Then $x\in L$ if and only if there is a number $u$ reachable by zero or more encoded $s$-window steps from the initial configuration code such that the code $u$, paired with $x$ and $s$, encodes a halted configuration with output $[\mathrm{true}]$.
